evidence.positive: Staged two demo-demo patients with hand-built operations via the admin API, then forced both operations to evaluation_mode='SILENT' by SQL (the entity default is INTERACTIVE, so an untouched hand-built case would have hidden the flip). Snapshotted row counts across all 99 demo-demo tables, then called GET /api/admin/patients/01a04494-e0eb-7689-8413-5070781d4ffb/operations/01a04494-e132-795e-bfc3-f0f4596b3984/context as admin with X-Tenant-Id: demo-demo. Got HTTP 200 with the full launch-context shape: patient (pmrn, dob 08/27/2008, age 18, height/weight, pediatricStatus ADULT), operation (caseId 51371, procedureTypes p-appendectomy, initialApplicationLaunchTime null), conditionProfile, integrationFailures []. Re-snapshotting all 99 tables showed exactly one behavioural change: audit_events grew by the VIEW_OPERATION row (the other new row was the script's own login). That row reads event_type=ADMIN_OPERATION, target_type=PATIENT, target=A-fake-d477c585-..., context={"caseId":"51371","action":"VIEW_OPERATION","operationId":"01a04494-e132-795e-bfc3-f0f4596b3984"}. Operation row after the read: evaluation_mode SILENT, initial_app_launch_time null, last_modified_date unchanged at 18:56:42.822624, operation_sessions 0, interactive_case_launch_events 0, operation_events 0.
evidence.negative: Three inverse cases, all against the running app. (1) Ownership: requested patient A's uuid with patient B's operation uuid -> HTTP 404 {"message":"Operation not found (01a04494-e170-7372-93a6-6ade42c59fe0)"}, no context body, and a full 99-table re-snapshot showed no VIEW_OPERATION audit row added (audit_events grew only by the two script logins; the VIEW_OPERATION count stayed at 1). A nonexistent operation uuid behaved identically. (2) Launch reporting: after the successful read, `select count(*) from audit_events where event_type='APP_LAUNCH'` returned 0, and `select distinct event_type` returned only ADMIN_OPERATION and RESOURCE_IMPORT, so the inspection is genuinely absent from launch reporting. (3) Access: the same URL as tenant user loopuser returned HTTP 403 Forbidden, and as admin under X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo returned HTTP 404, so the endpoint neither leaks to non-admins nor crosses tenants.
evidence.red_check: Data flip on the same operation. With operation 51371 back at SILENT / zero sessions / zero launch events, ran the real clinician path POST /api/app-launch {"patientId":"A-fake-d477c585-...","caseId":"51371"} as loopuser. Every absence assertion went red at once: evaluation_mode SILENT -> INTERACTIVE, initial_app_launch_time null -> 2026-08-27 18:58:40.504, interactive_case_launch_events 0 -> 1, operation_sessions 0 -> 1, patient_snapshots 0 -> 1, tracked_values 0 -> 1, user_case_activity_spans 0 -> 1, and an audit row event_type=APP_LAUNCH target=A-fake-d477c585-... context={"caseId":"51371"} appeared. The container log gained 'Case ID CaseId[value=51371] for Patient 01a04494-e0eb-7689-8413-5070781d4ffb already existed and was started' (grep count 1 over the whole log). Reverted by deleting the interactive_case_launch_events, user_case_activity_spans, tracked_values, patient_snapshots, operation_sessions and APP_LAUNCH audit rows and resetting evaluation_mode='SILENT', initial_app_launch_time=null, last_modified_date back to 18:56:42.822624. Re-ran the 99-table snapshot: identical to the post-read state again. Re-ran the positive GET afterwards: still HTTP 200, still SILENT, still 0 sessions / 0 launch events / 0 APP_LAUNCH audit rows.

red_check_signature: Case ID CaseId[value=51371] for Patient 01a04494-e0eb-7689-8413-5070781d4ffb already existed and was started
caveats: The container image ships no frontend assets (no index.html under /app), so every UI deliverable was unreachable: the View Operation button on the admin patient page, the /admin/patients/:patientUuid/operations/:operationUuid/debugger page, and the extracted DebuggerTabs with its lazy per-tab mounting were never rendered.

The 'Also fixed' frontend commits (leading slash on five API calls, the useFeatureFlag substring bug, the FeatureKey literal union) were therefore not exercised at all; the repo also has no frontend unit runner, so nothing covers them anywhere.
/api/feature-flags returns [] for demo-demo in this instance, so even the backend input that triggered the unknown-flag-id bug is absent here.

The case was hand-built through the admin API rather than arriving over HL7, and the demo tenant's EMR pull is synthesised from the existing operation row, so no real EMR integration was involved on either the read or the launch path.
The scope note holds: nothing was checked about whether the debugger tabs mutate the case once open, because the tabs never rendered.

automation.assessment: AppLaunchServiceTest and PatientControllerOperationContextTest already cover the service and controller well, but entirely with mocks: readOnlyContextLeavesTheCaseUntouched asserts verifyNoInteractions on the session/launch-event/audit collaborators and pins evaluationMode and initialAppLaunchTime on an in-memory entity, and the controller test pins the ADMIN_OPERATION audit shape including the null-caseId case. What no test covers is the claim at the level it actually matters: that a real HTTP GET against a persisted operation writes nothing to the database. Nothing covers the 403 for a non-admin, nothing covers tenant isolation, and nothing at all covers the frontend fixes.
proposed_tests: Integration test: GET the context endpoint for a persisted operation and assert the operation row is byte-for-byte unchanged (evaluation_mode, initial_app_launch_time, last_modified_date) and that operation_sessions and interactive_case_launch_events stay empty.
Integration test: assert the read writes exactly one audit_events row with event_type ADMIN_OPERATION and no row with event_type APP_LAUNCH.
Integration test: a non-admin session gets 403 on the context endpoint, and an admin under a different X-Tenant-Id gets 404.
Integration test: a 404 from a cross-patient operation uuid writes no audit row at all.

Frontend unit test once a runner exists (OR-2702): useFeatureFlags drops unknown ids from the response instead of returning [], and useFeatureFlag returns false for a key that is only a substring of the response body.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: The context endpoint returned the full launch-context shape for a persisted case, and a snapshot of all 99 tenant tables before and after showed the only change was one ADMIN_OPERATION audit row recording VIEW_OPERATION.

Negative: The case stayed in SILENT mode with no operation session, no interactive launch event and no APP_LAUNCH audit row, an operation belonging to a different patient returned 404 with no audit row written, a non-admin got 403 and a cross-tenant request got 404.

Red check: Running the real app launch on the same case turned every one of those absence checks red at once, including the mode flip to INTERACTIVE and the APP_LAUNCH audit row, and the state was reverted and the read re-confirmed clean.

Automation: The existing unit tests are mock-only, so integration coverage is proposed to prove at the HTTP level that the read writes nothing but its audit row.
